entities.summary:
Apollinaris the Elder, a Christian grammarian of the 4th century, left an indelible mark on the annals of history.











Born in unknown, Apollinaris rose to prominence as a scholar in Berytus, Phoenicia, and later in Laodicea, Syria, where he became a father figure to his son, Apollinaris of Laodicea.






Apollinaris's scholarly contributions focused on the interpretation of the New Testament, and his works on the subject remain influential to this day.











His impact on the development of Christian theology and the establishment of the Didache, a Christian scripture, solidify his place in the pantheon of Christian scholars.
